Questions and answers

What is Marque d’eaux sûres?

In this glossary, Marque d’eaux sûres refers to: IALA buoyage mark indicating there is navigable water all around the mark.

How is Marque d’eaux sûres used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "VTS au navire : 'Avancez jusqu’à la marque d’eaux sûres et signalez quand vous êtes abeam.'"

Why does Marque d’eaux sûres matter in maritime?

Marque d’eaux sûres matters because it supports clear communication in Nav contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Marque d’eaux sûres?

Marque d’eaux sûres is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.
